title: Compatibility: Chat Completions request shaper with SSE streaming & function-call coalescing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a compatibility layer that maps legacy OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response semantics onto Redwood's streaming-first runtime while preserving expected tool/function-calling behavior and structured outputs. This includes: SSE framing (data: chunks + [DONE]), partial function call deltas, role/metadata preservation, idempotency hints, and deterministic ordering for mixed streaming & non-streaming clients.
acceptance_criteria: SSE stream framing conforms to OpenAI clients: initial data chunks contain incremental "

All function call invocations can start streaming partial args and finish with a final function call event; clients expecting a single final function call object receive an equivalent assembled object.
Non-streaming requests receive identical aggregated JSON response shape to legacy API for a broad set of test prompts (n=250), including tool calls and structured outputs.
Telemetry emitted for each compatibility transformation (request_shaper.v1, function_coalesce.v1) and no >1% error-rate regression after rollout.
Backward-compat regression tests added to CI and a canary rollout plan defined in the rollout notes.
notes: 2026-02-10 — Triage: Identified customer reports where legacy clients expect a single final function_call object but new runtime streams partial function args as deltas; causes client-side JSON parse errors.
2026-02-15 — Spec drafted: three-mode shaper (strict, permissive, streaming-first). Document: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/compat/cc-request-shaper (internal).

2026-02-22 — Design review: decided to implement server-side coalescer that buffers function-call deltas up to N ms or until completion marker; default N=150ms. Trade-off: small added latency for deterministic compatibility vs. complexity managing backpressure.
2026-02-28 — Implementation started: core transforms in gateway (request normalization, role mapping, tool_call hooks). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3421

2026-03-03 — QA: added fuzz tests for mixed streaming + tool-call sequences; discovered edge case where two concurrent function calls interleave — added per-conversation function-call namespace to avoid cross-talk.
2026-03-07 — Performance: bench shows 2-4% p99 latency delta under heavy batching when coalescing enabled; added opt-out flag for dedicated customers (compat.mode=strict) and runtime telemetry.
2026-03-10 — In Progress: finishing integration tests and adding canary rollout steps. Next: security review if customers request KMS-backed tool-call payloads.

Implementation notes: use event types 'delta', 'func_start', 'func_arg', 'func_end' in internal stream; transform to OpenAI SSE by emitting 'data: {"choices":[{"delta":...}]}' chunks, and a final 'data: [DONE]'. Buffering is bounded and fallbacks to passthrough under heavy backpressure.
Rollout plan: canary 1% of hosted traffic for 48h, monitor compatibility-errors, p99 latency, and function_call assembly rate. If errors < 0.5% and latency < +5%, expand to 25% then 100%.
